section_summary.extract_value: This section introduces two types of global self-evaluation: self-competence and self-liking, which are distinct constructs measured by the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale (RSES). Self-competence is based on successful goal pursuit, while self-liking is a subjective evaluation of personal worth. The current studies explored the relationships among self-competence, self-liking, the RSES, and self-deception using multiple regression and a trait-profile approach, predicting that self-competence would be less susceptible to self-deception contamination compared to self-liking.
